atoms.a: Pharaohs wore a special headdress called a Nemes.
atoms.sound: Pharaohs wore a special headdress called a Nemmez.

atoms.a: Pharaohs wore a fake beard to make themselves look like the gods. Even the female pharaohs wore one!
Pharaohs often held a shepherd’s crook — a long stick with a hook at the end — to symbolise the pharaoh looking after their own flock: the Egyptian people.
Pharaohs also held a flail — a tool used for farming grain — to symbolise how the pharaoh provided for the people.

atoms.b: ((++Symbols spells)) were very important for showing the power of the pharaoh. One of the most important symbols was the double ((++crown cow)) of Egypt.
The double crown was made by combining two separate crowns. The first was the ((++red green)) crown of Lower Egypt.
The second crown was the ((++white brown)) crown of Upper Egypt. The pharaoh would wear the different crowns while in the appropriate ((++area time)) of Egypt.

feedback.end: Death masks were expensive, golden masks made to look like the pharaoh. The Egyptians believed that the souls of dead pharaohs returned to their bodies at night, and the mask was used to help them identify the right one!
Statues of themselves were important for pharaohs to demonstrate their wealth and power across all of Egypt.
The ankh was a symbol used to represent the life-giving powers of the pharaoh.
